episode_title: Episode 137: Own Your Seat with AlexSandra Sisler

real_qa.q: What is AlexSandra Sisler's Own Your Seat movement and what does EmpowerServe offer?
real_qa.r: Own Your Seat is a movement and platform bringing together leadership development, retail strategy, and customer experience. Through it, Sisler wants women to recognize their value, own their contributions and have a voice in decisions shaping their futures. EmpowerServe is the company platform that houses this work, and Sisler is currently writing a book on Own Your Seat to continue the message beyond traditional self-help into practical direction for people pursuing opportunities.
real_qa.requete: Own Your Seat AlexSandra Sisler EmpowerServe

real_qa.q: What skincare revenue did AlexSandra Sisler generate in the physician-dispensed boutique's first year?
real_qa.r: The physician-dispensed skincare boutique that Sisler helped develop generated 1.8 million in skincare revenue in its first year. She developed skincare retail strategies with a plastic surgeon that helped grow the practice before opening this boutique.
real_qa.requete: 1.8 million skincare revenue first year boutique

real_qa.q: What is the snowballing team development technique AlexSandra Sisler recommends for building clinic culture?
real_qa.r: Snowballing consists of short 15-minute shadowing opportunities across departments where employees follow colleagues to understand their roles—for example, an NP following a patient coordinator or an MA following the billing specialist. These carved-out shadowing periods naturally create higher emotional intelligence within the clinic or practice.

real_qa.q: Why do practice managers fail by working behind closed doors instead of on the clinic floor?
real_qa.r: When managers spend their days behind closed doors, they lose connection with the patient journey and cannot manage the patient experience. Managers need to be on the floor every 15 minutes to two hours, observing phones, checkout, retail, and employee interactions—greeting patients, stepping into treatment rooms, and truly leading. Without this visibility and involvement, they make decisions about parts of the business they don't understand.
real_qa.requete: practice manager floor visibility patient experience management

real_qa.q: How many practices did AlexSandra Sisler support as VP of Aesthetics at Platinum Dermatology Partners?
real_qa.r: As VP of Aesthetics at Platinum Dermatology Partners, Sisler supported 125 practices nationally, working alongside her colleague Chris Murray to manage aesthetics operations across this large network.
real_qa.requete: Platinum Dermatology Partners 125 practices VP Aesthetics

guest.bio_context: AlexSandra Sisler has worked in aesthetics since age 15, starting at Merle Norman Cosmetics before moving through retail leadership at Bath and Body Works, clinic operations at American Laser, and plastic surgery practice management. She developed skincare retail strategies that generated 1.8 million in skincare revenue in the first year of a physician-dispensed boutique, then moved to Revision Skin Care as Skincare Strategy Manager before becoming VP of Aesthetics at Platinum Dermatology Partners, where she supported 125 practices nationally alongside colleague Chris Murray. She is now building EmpowerServe and the Own Your Seat platform focused on leadership development, retail strategy, and customer experience.

real_quote: I didn't fight my way to the table just to hand it over for someone else to use my voice.
